fullPassage:
Wheels of Adventures

A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"

Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.

Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot that appears in most movies and TV shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset.

The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to fuel up for a hike.

While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.

Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture!

Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife. Watching people floating down the Merced River and hiking the Half Dome was cool. It was indeed a wonderful trip, with lots of laughter, joy, and sweat.

I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only (A)[companions / competitors] would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of (B)[challenges / comforts] we would face, but Dan (C)[assured / alarmed] me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 나의 유일한 동반자(companions)는 친한 친구 Dan과 휠체어일 것이다. 어떤 도전(challenges)에 직면할지 확신이 없었지만, Dan은 우리가 가장 멋진 여행자가 될 거라고 확신시켜 주었다(assured).
det.analysis:
✅ ② companions — challenges — assured: 원문 일치
❌ ① competitors(경쟁자): 친구와 휠체어는 '경쟁자'가 아닌 '동반자'
❌ ③ comforts(안락함): 불확실함을 나타내는 문맥에서 '안락함'은 부적절, alarmed(불안하게 하다): assured의 반의어
❌ ④ competitors + comforts: 둘 다 부적절
det.tip: companion(동반자) ↔ competitor(경쟁자), challenge(도전) ↔ comfort(안락), assure(확신시키다) ↔ alarm(불안하게 하다)

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an (A)[extensive / limited] public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars do not (B)[accommodate / exclude] wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us (C)[aboard / ashore], and we were off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 도시는 광범위한(extensive) 대중교통 시스템을 갖추고 있다. 역사적인 케이블카가 휠체어 사용자를 수용하지(accommodate) 않는다는 것을 알게 되어 실망했다. 친절한 운전사가 우리를 탑승(aboard)하도록 환영했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① extensive — accommodate — aboard: 원문 일치
❌ ② limited(제한된): extensive(광범위한)의 반의어
❌ ③ exclude(배제하다): accommodate(수용하다)의 반의어, ashore(해안으로): aboard(탑승하여)와 다른 의미
❌ ④ limited + exclude: 둘 다 반의어
det.tip: extensive(광범위한) ↔ limited(제한된), accommodate(수용하다) ↔ exclude(배제하다), aboard(탑승하여) ↔ ashore(해안으로)

questions.passage: The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park. The park is famous for Northern California's natural (A)[scenery / industry] of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery (B)[gradually / suddenly] changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant. It was (C)[massive / miniature], and I felt quite small in comparison.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 공원은 북부 캘리포니아의 자연 경관(scenery)으로 유명하다. 경관이 점차(gradually) 도시에서 교외, 숲, 산으로 변하는 것을 보았다. 그것은 거대했고(massive), 나는 비교적 꽤 작게 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ scenery — gradually — massive: 원문 일치
❌ ① suddenly(갑자기): 도시→교외→숲→산 순차적 변화이므로 gradually가 적합
❌ ② industry(산업): 폭포, 계곡, 숲은 자연 경관이지 산업이 아님, miniature(소형의): massive의 반의어
❌ ④ industry + suddenly: 둘 다 부적절
det.tip: scenery(경관) ↔ industry(산업), gradually(점차) ↔ suddenly(갑자기), massive(거대한) ↔ miniature(소형의)

questions.passage: They didn't smell ①<u>pleasant</u> up close, yet their cuteness ②<u>delayed</u> our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge. We took a ③<u>cruise</u>, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer ④<u>drought</u> blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다리를 지날 때 여름 산들바람(breeze)이 천천히 불었다. drought(가뭄)는 breeze(산들바람)와 전혀 다른 의미이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ drought(가뭄) → breeze(산들바람)가 원문. '바람이 불었다'는 문맥에 drought는 부적절
❌ ① pleasant(쾌적한): 원문 그대로
❌ ② delayed(지연시켰다): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ cruise(유람선): 원문 그대로
det.tip: breeze(산들바람) ≠ drought(가뭄). blew(불다)의 주어로 breeze가 자연스러움

questions.passage: While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant. It was ①<u>massive</u>, and I felt quite small in ②<u>comparison</u>. As we made our way down a trail, we ③<u>avoided</u> a black bear. It began to ④<u>approach</u> us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산길을 내려가다가 검은 곰을 마주쳤다(encountered). avoided(피했다)는 encountered(마주쳤다)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ avoided(피했다) → encountered(마주쳤다)가 원문. 곰과 대면한 상황이므로 avoided는 부적절
❌ ① massive(거대한): 원문 그대로
❌ ② comparison(비교): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ approach(다가가다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: encounter(마주치다) ↔ avoid(피하다). 곰을 만났다는 사건 전개에서 encountered가 적합

questions.passage: Dan found out that the National Park offers hand-crank bikes. Dan ①<u>discouraged</u> me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a ②<u>masterpiece</u> painted by Mother Nature. I was ③<u>fortunate</u> to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were ④<u>obstacles</u> to overcome and challenges to meet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: Dan은 내가 하나를 시도해 보도록 설득했다(persuaded). discouraged(낙담시켰다)는 persuaded(설득했다)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① discouraged(낙담시켰다) → persuaded(설득했다)가 원문. '곧 잘 사용할 수 있었다'는 긍정적 결과와 discouraged는 모순
❌ ② masterpiece(걸작): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ fortunate(행운의): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ obstacles(장애물): 원문 그대로
det.tip: persuade(설득하다) ↔ discourage(낙담시키다). 뒤 문장(곧 잘 할 수 있었다)이 긍정적 → persuaded가 적합

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was __________ to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 여행 중 Dan과 Roy 아저씨 같은 동반자가 있어서 행운이었다(fortunate).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ fortunate(행운인): 좋은 동반자를 가졌다는 긍정적 문맥에 적합
❌ ① unfortunate(불운한): 긍정적 문맥에 반의어
❌ ② reluctant(꺼리는): 동반자에 대한 감사 표현과 부적합
❌ ③ anxious(불안한): 긍정적 회상 문맥과 부적합
det.tip: fortunate(행운인) ↔ unfortunate(불운한). be fortunate to V = ~하게 되어 행운이다

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not __________ wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 역사적인 케이블카가 휠체어 사용자를 수용하지(accommodate) 않는다는 것을 알게 되어 실망했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ accommodate(수용하다): 휠체어 사용자를 탑승시킬 수 없다는 문맥에 적합
❌ ① transport(운송하다): 문맥상 '수용/지원'의 의미가 더 적절
❌ ② prohibit(금지하다): 원문은 '수용하지 않는다'이지 '금지한다'가 아님
❌ ④ abandon(버리다): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: accommodate = 수용하다, 편의를 제공하다. '장애인을 위한 시설/서비스'를 제공한다는 의미로 자주 사용

questions.passage: The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery __________ changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to fuel up for a hike.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 동쪽으로 향하면서, 우리는 풍경이 도시에서 교외로, 숲으로, 마침내 산으로 서서히(gradually) 변하는 것을 보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② gradually(서서히): 도시→교외→숲→산 순차적 단계별 변화에 적합
❌ ① abruptly(갑자기): 단계별 변화에 부적합
❌ ③ dramatically(극적으로): 순차적 점진 변화에 과한 표현
❌ ④ permanently(영구적으로): 시각적 변화를 묘사하는 문맥에 부적합
det.tip: gradually(점진적으로) ↔ abruptly(갑자기). from A to B, to C, to D 구조 = 순차적 전환 → gradually

questions.passage: I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan <u>assured</u> me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, Dan shouted, 'Let's get rolling!'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 assured와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: Dan은 우리가 가장 멋진 여행자가 될 거라고 확신시켜 주었다(assured).
det.analysis:
✅ ① guaranteed(보장했다): assured의 동의어. 확신을 심어주다는 의미
❌ ② questioned(의문을 제기했다): assured의 반의어적 뉘앙스
❌ ③ warned(경고했다): 긍정적 확신과 반대
❌ ④ confused(혼란시켰다): assured의 반의어
det.tip: assure = guarantee = 확신시키다, 보장하다. assure + 사람 + that절 = ~에게 ~을 확신시키다

questions.passage: While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was <u>massive</u>, and I felt quite small in comparison.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 massive와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그것은 거대했고(massive), 나는 비교적 꽤 작게 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ enormous(거대한): massive의 동의어. 크기가 압도적이라는 의미
❌ ① ancient(고대의): 나이에 관한 단어, 크기와 무관
❌ ② beautiful(아름다운): 외관에 관한 단어, 크기와 무관
❌ ③ fragile(부서지기 쉬운): massive의 반의어적 뉘앙스
det.tip: massive = enormous = huge = immense (거대한). 'felt quite small in comparison'이 크기를 나타내는 단서

questions.passage: As we made our way down a trail, we <u>encountered</u> a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 encountered와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 산길을 내려가다가 검은 곰을 마주쳤다(encountered).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ came across(우연히 만나다): encountered의 동의어. 예상치 못한 만남
❌ ① avoided(피했다): encountered의 반의어
❌ ② expected(예상했다): 마주친 것이지 예상한 것이 아님
❌ ④ chased(쫓았다): 곰을 마주친 것이지 쫓은 것이 아님
det.tip: encounter = come across = run into = 우연히 마주치다. 예상치 못한 만남을 강조

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an <u>extensive</u> public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars do not accommodate wheelchair users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 extensive와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 이 도시는 광범위한(extensive) 대중교통 시스템을 갖추고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② limited(제한된): extensive의 반의어
❌ ① broad(넓은): extensive의 동의어
❌ ③ wide(넓은): extensive의 동의어
❌ ④ vast(광대한): extensive의 동의어
det.tip: extensive(광범위한) = broad = wide = vast ↔ limited(제한된) = restricted = narrow

questions.passage: All I needed to take with me was <u>courage</u>. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future. I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 courage와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 내가 가져가야 할 것은 오직 용기(courage)뿐이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ cowardice(비겁함): courage의 반의어
❌ ① bravery(용감함): courage의 동의어
❌ ② boldness(대담함): courage의 동의어
❌ ③ valor(용맹): courage의 동의어
det.tip: courage(용기) = bravery = boldness = valor ↔ cowardice(비겁함) = timidity(소심함)

questions.passage:
(A) It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to <u>approach</u> us.

(B) The teacher suggested a new <u>approach</u> to solving the math problem.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 approach의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 곰이 우리에게 다가오기(approach) 시작했다. (B) 선생님은 수학 문제를 풀기 위한 새로운 접근법(approach)을 제안했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 다가가다 — 접근법: (A) 동사로 '다가오다', (B) 명사로 '접근법/방법'
❌ ① 접근법 — 다가가다: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 접근법 — 접근법: (A)에서 approach는 동사로 사용
❌ ④ 다가가다 — 다가가다: (B)에서 approach는 명사로 사용
det.tip: approach 다의어: ① 동사: 다가가다, 접근하다 ② 명사: 접근법, 방법. a new approach to = ~에 대한 새로운 접근법

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the general appearance of an area of land, especially its natural features"

det.korean: 어떤 지역의 전반적인 모습, 특히 자연적 특징 = 경치/풍경(scenery)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ scenery(경치): 정의에 정확히 부합. 자연 경관의 전반적 모습
❌ ① suburb(교외): 도시 외곽 지역, 자연 경관과 다른 개념
❌ ② wildlife(야생동물): 동물에 관한 단어, 지역 외관과 무관
❌ ④ obstacle(장애물): 방해물이지 경관이 아님
det.tip: scenery = 경치, 풍경. natural scenery = 자연 경관. scene(장면)에서 파생

questions.passage: It was massive, and I felt quite small in __________ (compare). We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그것은 거대했고, 비교하면(in comparison) 나는 꽤 작게 느꼈다.
det.analysis: compare(동사: 비교하다) → comparison(명사: 비교). in 뒤에 명사가 필요하므로 명사형으로 변환.
det.tip: compare(v. 비교하다) → comparison(n. 비교). in comparison = 비교해 보면. 전치사 in 뒤 → 명사형

questions.passage: Dan __________ (persuasion) me to try a hand-crank bike, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: Dan이 나를 핸드크랭크 자전거를 타 보도록 설득했다(persuaded).
det.analysis: persuasion(명사: 설득) → persuaded(동사 과거형: 설득했다). 주어 Dan 뒤에 동사가 필요하고, 과거 시제이므로 과거형 -ed.
det.tip: persuasion(n. 설득) → persuade(v. 설득하다) → persuaded(과거형). 명사→동사 과거형 변환. persuade + 사람 + to V = ~에게 ~하도록 설득하다

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were __________ to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 극복해야 할 장애물(obstacles)이 있었고 직면해야 할 도전이 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacles(장애물): overcome(극복하다)과 자연스러운 연어 관계. 모험에 어려움이 따른다는 문맥
❌ ② advantages(이점): overcome(극복하다)과 어울리지 않음
❌ ③ shortcuts(지름길): 극복 대상이 아님
❌ ④ celebrations(축하): 극복 대상이 아님
det.tip: obstacles to overcome = 극복해야 할 장애물. overcome obstacles는 고정 연어. obstacle ↔ advantage

questions.passage: Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to __________. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 곰이 우리가 싸 온 음식 냄새를 맡았기 때문에 우리에게 다가오기(approach us) 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② approach us(우리에게 다가오다): 음식 냄새를 맡고 다가온다는 문맥에 적합. Uncle Roy가 돌을 던진 이유
❌ ① run away from us(도망치다): 음식 냄새에 끌려온 것이지 도망친 것이 아님
❌ ③ hide behind a tree(나무 뒤에 숨다): 음식에 관심을 보이는 행동과 부적합
❌ ④ climb up a rock(바위를 오르다): 다가오는 위험 상황과 무관
det.tip: approach = 다가가다/접근하다. because 절의 원인(음식 냄새)과 결과(다가옴)의 논리적 연결이 핵심
